A Joint Score-Driven Filter

Source: R/gas_joint.R
GasJoint.Rd

The S7 class of several gas() terms that sit in the equations of different distribution parameters and are filtered as one recursion. Build one with gas_joint().

Usage

GasJoint(
  label = character(0),
  hyper = list(),
  grid = list(),
  values = list(),
  min_ratio = numeric(0),
  search = character(0),
  ids = character(0),
  build_info = list(),
  terms = list(),
  params = character(0),
  offsets = integer(0),
  partners = list(),
  keys = character(0)
)

Arguments

label

A character string prefixed to the term's coefficient names when non-empty, and used as the title of plot() and the tag of print(). The empty string "" means no label.

hyper

The hyperparameters of the term's penalty that the caller held, as a named list keyed by the penalty's names. Empty, the default, means every one of them is estimated. See term_hyper().

grid

How many values a path visits for each of the term's hyperparameters, as a named list of single whole numbers. Empty, the default, leaves the number to the fitting layer. See term_grid().

values

The values that a path visits, for each hyperparameter that the caller wrote out, as a named list of numeric vectors. Empty, the default, has the path build them. See term_values().

min_ratio

How far down the path over the size of the kink reaches, as a fraction of the value that empties the block: one number in \((0, 1)\), or numeric(0) for the fitting layer's own. See term_path_min().

search

How the term's own hyperparameters are covered when it has more than one carrying a kink: "grid" for every combination of them, "cyclic" for one at a time, or character(0) for the default. See term_search().

ids

Which of the term's hyperparameters are shared with those of other terms, and under what label: a character vector named by the term's own hyperparameters, or character(0) for none. The terms carrying the same label for the same hyperparameter estimate one value. See term_ids().

build_info

The shared ordering: order (the rows of each group, in time order) and n. The property is inherited from structural_term().

terms

A named list of built GasTerm() objects, one per filtered parameter, named by the parameter.

params

The names of the filtered parameters, in the order of terms.

offsets

The position before the first parameter of each term in the joint parameter vector.

partners

A list with one integer vector per term: the positions in params of the parameters whose scores the term's level loads besides its own.

keys

The names under which a fitting layer knew each term before joining them, named by the parameter, or an empty vector.

Value

An S7 object of class GasJoint, inheriting from structural_term(), so that a fitting layer treats the joint filter as one structural term whose parameters are those of its terms, each prefixed by the distribution parameter of its term.

Details

A score-driven level in the equation of one parameter is driven by the score of that parameter, which is evaluated at the current values of all the others. Where two parameters both carry a level, each score depends on the other level, so the two recursions are one: with \(G\) the filtered parameters, $$f_{k,t} = \omega_k + \sum_{i=1}^{p_k} \kappa_{k,i}\, u_{k,t-i} + \sum_{l \in C_k} \sum_{i=1}^{p_{kl}} \kappa_{k,i,l}\, u_{l,t-i} + \sum_{j=1}^{q_k} \xi_{k,j} f_{k,t-j}, \qquad k \in G,$$ where \(u_t\) is the vector of driving scores of the parameters in \(G\), read at the predictor of every equation at time \(t\), \(C_k\) is the set of the parameters to which the p_cross of the term of \(k\) gives a positive count, and \(p_{kl}\) is that count. The persistence of each level is its own, so the autoregressive part is stationary when each equation's is.

The driving vector is the caller's: a fitting layer supplies \(u_t = \mathcal{I}_{GG,t}^{-d}\,\partial\ell_t/\partial\eta_{G,t}\) with the expected information of the filtered parameters and its derivative in the predictors.

See also

gas_joint(), the constructor; gas() for one term.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(t = 1:40, y = rnorm(40))
tm <- list(mu = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t), dd),
           sigma = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t), dd))
jt <- gas_joint(tm)
S7::S7_inherits(jt, GasJoint)
#> [1] TRUE
jt@params
#> [1] "mu"    "sigma"
